about.title: Built for health stress and everyday calm
about.body: CalmIq helps individuals manage health-related stress: soothing check-ins, simple calm routines, and recovery-comfort ideas (rest, pacing, gentle self-massage or actuator-style comfort guidance). Chat is a companion, not a clinic — when hands-on care matters, Calm+ members can request a physiotherapist session.
about.disclaimer: CalmIq does not diagnose, treat, or replace professional medical advice. Seek urgent care for severe or sudden symptoms.

routines.title: Calm routines
routines.support: Short guided flows for everyday stress — wellness support, not medical care.
routines.doneBody: Take what felt useful. You can repeat this anytime, or chat if you want to unpack how you feel.
routines.disclaimer: These routines are general wellbeing tools for stress and comfort. They are not medical treatment, diagnosis, or a substitute for professional care. Stop if anything feels wrong, and seek urgent help for severe or sudden symptoms. Physiotherapist sessions stay on Calm+ separately.

breathing.title: Breathing reset
breathing.intent: A longer-exhale pattern to ease stress in about two minutes.

s1.title: Settle in
s1.body: Sit or stand comfortably. Soften your jaw and drop your shoulders. You will breathe with a slightly longer exhale — a simple way to signal calm, not a medical exercise.

s2.title: Longer exhale
s2.body: Inhale gently for 4, hold for 2, exhale slowly for 6. Repeat for a few cycles. Keep the breath quiet and easy — no forcing.

s3.title: Notice
s3.body: Pause. Feel your feet or the chair. Notice any ease without judging what is still tense.

s4.title: Easy rhythm
s4.body: Inhale for 4, exhale for 6, a few more times. Let the out-breath be the longest part.

s5.title: Close
s5.body: Return to your natural breath. Carry one slower exhale into the next moment of your day.

desk-reset.title: Desk reset
desk-reset.intent: Stand, loosen shoulders, rest your eyes, and take a short walk cue.

s1.title: Step away briefly
s1.body: Save your work if you need to. This is a short comfort break for desk stress — not physio or medical advice.

s2.title: Stand
s2.body: Stand up if you can. Plant both feet. Uncross your legs and let your arms hang for a moment.

s3.title: Shoulders
s3.body: Gently roll your shoulders up, back, and down a few times. Keep the range small and comfortable.

s4.title: Eyes
s4.body: Look away from the screen toward something farther away. Blink slowly a few times, then soften your gaze.

s5.title: Short walk cue
s5.body: If you can, walk to another room or along a short path. Even a minute of movement helps reset desk tension.

s6.title: Return gently
s6.body: When you sit again, keep one easy shoulder drop and a slower breath. Come back anytime you feel wound up at the desk.

wind-down.title: Wind-down
wind-down.intent: An evening downshift with lights, breath, and parking the phone.

s1.title: Evening pause
s1.body: This is a gentle wind-down for the day — wellbeing comfort, not sleep medicine or clinical care.

s2.title: Softer light
s2.body: Dim bright screens or lamps if you can. Aim for calmer light so your body gets an “evening” cue.

s3.title: Slow breath
s3.body: Inhale for 4, hold for 4, exhale for 8. A few quiet cycles — longer out-breaths, no strain.

s4.title: Phone park
s4.body: Place your phone face down or out of arm’s reach for a few minutes. You can return to it after this routine.

s5.title: Stillness
s5.body: Sit or lie comfortably. Notice the room around you. Let thoughts pass without chasing them.

s6.title: One more soft breath
s6.body: Inhale for 4, exhale for 8, a few times. Keep it lazy and quiet.

s7.title: Rest cue
s7.body: End here. Keep the softer light and slower breath into whatever comes next — rest, reading, or sleep when you are ready.
